skill.name: define-my-content-pillars
skill.description: Work out the three to five subjects someone can post about repeatedly without running dry, from what they have already published and what they actually know. Use when someone asks what they should post about, says they have run out of ideas, wants content pillars or themes, or is starting an account and does not know where to aim. Do not use it to plan dates or write posts.
skill.summary: Identify focused content pillars from a creator's experience, existing posts, audience needs, and distinctive point of view.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.value_statement: Creators often choose broad topics and run out of useful ideas. This skill turns their experience, posts, and audience needs into focused content pillars.
actual_capabilities: Collects existing posts, expertise, audience needs, and desired reputation as planning evidence.
Groups existing posts by subject and identifies gaps between intended and actual topics.
Tests candidate pillars for depth, first-hand knowledge, audience demand, and distinctiveness.
Defines three to five focused pillars with an angle, seed ideas, and clear boundaries.
Identifies subjects to stop posting about when they lack experience, demand, or differentiation.
limitations: It does not create a dated publishing calendar.
It does not write complete social media posts.
Recommendations depend on the quality and breadth of the provided evidence.
Connected analytics and voice insights require an available VoiceMOAT integration and plan.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Personal Brand
use_cases.description: Turn your past posts, expertise, and audience goals into a small set of recognizable content themes.

use_cases.title: Restart a Stalled Account
use_cases.description: Find durable subjects and fresh seed ideas when your current content process repeatedly runs out of direction.
use_cases.target_user: Creators with inactive or inconsistent accounts

use_cases.title: Shape a New Content Direction
use_cases.description: Evaluate possible topics against audience needs and first-hand experience before committing to a new account theme.
use_cases.target_user: Founders and subject-matter experts starting an account

prompt_templates.title: Start With My Background
prompt_templates.prompt: I am starting a content account. Ask me about my work, experience, audience, and opinions, then suggest three possible content pillars.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Existing Posts
prompt_templates.prompt: Here are my last 15 posts: [paste posts]. Group them by subject, show the actual distribution, and identify the three strongest recurring themes.

prompt_templates.title: Test Candidate Pillars
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these candidate pillars: [list pillars]. For each, test depth, first-hand knowledge, audience demand, and distinctiveness. Explain which fail and why.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Focused Pillar Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Using my posts, expertise, audience, and goals below, define three to five content pillars. Give each a definition, unique angle, five seed ideas, and one boundary. Also name subjects I should drop.

output_examples.input: I am a product marketer who has written about launches, customer interviews, and team processes.
output: Customer research that changes product decisions
Practical launch lessons from small teams

output_examples.input: Most of my posts discuss software tools, although I want to be known for hiring advice.
output_examples.output: Your strongest evidence supports a tooling and workflow pillar. Keep hiring only if you can provide first-hand examples and a specific perspective; otherwise, pause it until your experience supports a deeper body of work.

best_practices: Provide ten to fifteen ordinary past posts instead of only your strongest examples.
State who you want to help and what those readers need.
Use first-hand experience and audience response to narrow broad topics.
anti_patterns: Choosing broad labels such as marketing instead of specific subjects and angles.
Selecting pillars only because they sound interesting without testing audience demand.
Asking for a posting calendar when you still lack a clear set of themes.

faq.question: How many content pillars should I choose?
faq.answer: Choose three to five. Fewer can become repetitive, while more can make your account difficult to recognize.

faq.question: What if I have not published anything yet?
faq.answer: Use your work, recurring questions from others, and subjects you can discuss from direct experience.

faq.question: Should a pillar be a broad industry?
faq.answer: Usually no. A useful pillar combines a specific subject with your experience and a clear audience need.

faq.question: Does this skill create post ideas?
faq.answer: It creates seed ideas for each agreed pillar. It does not write complete posts.

faq.question: Does this skill plan my publishing schedule?
faq.answer: No. It defines the themes first. Use a separate planning workflow to assign dates and formats.

faq.question: Can connected analytics improve the result?
faq.answer: Yes. Available post history, engagement, and voice insights can make the pillar recommendations more evidence-based.
